commitResults.messageBody: Add echo functionality for Lebron
Users can now use LeBron to keep track and list items.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add mark and unmark functionality for list
commitResults.messageBody: LeBron can now mark and unmark tasks for users. A task class is introduced, allowing LeBron to modify and mark/unmark tasks.

LeBron can now handle 3 different Task types - Todo, Deadline and Event, all of which extend Task.

Todo is a Task with no other parameters.

Deadline is a Task with a due date.

Event is a Task with a start and end time.
LeBron can now handle errors such as marking/unmarking tasks that do not exist, unrecognised inputs or giving blank statements following Task declarations.
LeBron can now delete tasks. Also changed Tasks to be stored in Java's ArrayList, instead of a local size 100 array.
Previously input string was manually detected using massive else-if blocks. It is changed to now use an enum called CommandType, used to group input types together.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add ability to save and load TaskList using Storage
Support dates and times for Tasks
Extract Ui, Parser, TaskList, Storage for A-MoreOOP
commitResults.messageBody:
LeBron now constructs Ui/Storage/TaskList once and delegates user I/O
to Ui, command interpretation and argument extraction to Parser, and
task list/persistence to TaskList/Storage, instead of doing everything
inline in main().

commitResults.messageTitle: Divide classes into packages and add Command pattern for A-Packages
commitResults.messageBody:
Organizes all classes into packages by responsibility (lebron.task,
lebron.parser, lebron.ui, lebron.storage, lebron.exception,
lebron.command), and introduces a Command interface so Parser returns
an executable Command instead of a CommandType, replacing LeBron.run()'s
switch statement with polymorphic dispatch. Also removes the unused
Time.java stub.

The mainClass was left as the template placeholder seedu.duke.Duke
after merging add-gradle-support, which doesn't exist in this
project and would make `gradlew run` fail with a
ClassNotFoundException. Point it at the actual entry point instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Accept the save file path via constructor
commitResults.messageBody:
The path was hardcoded to data/LeBron.txt, so there was no way to
point Storage at an isolated file in a test without touching real
save data. Add a Storage(Path) constructor for that; the existing
no-arg constructor keeps defaulting to data/LeBron.txt, so LeBron.java
needs no changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for A-JUnit increment
commitResults.messageBody:
Covers Parser (every command type's happy path plus every documented
failure mode), TaskList (boundary conditions and defensive copying),
Storage (real save/load round-trip via @TempDir), all Command classes
(execute() including exception paths), and Task/Todo/Deadline/Event
formatting. Uses a hand-written StubUi test double instead of a
mocking framework to keep Command tests readable and decoupled from
Ui's printed text.

Also documents the 50% test-coverage target and stub/@TempDir
convention in AGENTS.md so future changes keep tests in sync.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add missing Javadoc to reach full non-private coverage
commitResults.messageBody:
LeBron, LeBronException, TaskListException, and CommandType had no
class-level Javadoc, and LeBron's constructor/run()/main() were also
undocumented, leaving them as the only non-private classes/methods in
the codebase without header comments.

While generating Javadoc to verify these additions, the build failed
on two invalid @return tags in Ui (used on void methods), and Storage
save() was missing a required @throws for its declared IOException;
both are fixed here so `./gradlew javadoc` succeeds cleanly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tweak code to comply with SE-EDU Java coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
Brought the codebase in line with se-education.org/guides/conventions/java:
- Add the missing space before opening braces on method/constructor/class
  headers in Ui, Task, Todo, Event, and LeBronException (K&R style requires
  it; some of these used "){" with no space).
- Add spaces around the ternary operator in Task.toString().
- Deadline.toString() and Event.toString() exceeded the 120-char hard line
  length limit (up to 193 chars). Extracted the repeated
  DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("MMM d yyyy") call into a shared
  DISPLAY_DATE_FORMAT constant in each class and wrapped Event's line,
  which also removes the duplicated formatter construction and a stray
  double space that had crept into the concatenation.

Going forward, new code added to this project should follow this standard
by default.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command to search tasks by keyword
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds "find KEYWORD", which lists tasks whose description contains the
given keyword (case-insensitive substring match), so a user with a long
list doesn't have to scroll through it to find one item.

- Task gains getDescription() so TaskList can search on it without
  parsing toString()'s display format.
- TaskList.findTasks(keyword) does the filtering, keeping matches in
  their original order.
- FindCommand + a new FIND CommandType/Parser case wire it into the
  existing command flow; a missing/blank keyword throws LeBronException
  like the other commands (todo, deadline, event) do.
- Ui.showMatchingTasks() reuses the numbered-list style already used by
  showTaskList/TaskList.toString() for a consistent look.

Covered by new tests in TaskListTest, FindCommandTest, and ParserTest.

Adds missing Javadoc to LeBron, LeBronException, TaskListException, and
CommandType, and fixes two invalid @return tags plus a missing @throws
that broke ./gradlew javadoc.

Fixes K&R brace spacing, ternary operator spacing, and two over-length
lines to comply with the SE-EDU Java coding standard.

# Conflicts:
#	src/main/java/lebron/exception/LeBronException.java

Adds the find command: lists tasks whose description contains a given
keyword (Level-9 increment).

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JavaFX GUI to LeBron chatbot
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds a JavaFX GUI (Level 10) so the chatbot can be used through a
window instead of only the console. Parts 1-4 of the SE-EDU JavaFX
tutorial were completed beforehand in a separate sandbox project.

- Command.execute() and every Ui.showXxx() method now build and
  return the response as a String instead of printing it via
  System.out. This was needed because the GUI has to put the same
  reply into a chat bubble rather than a terminal; making Ui a pure
  message builder lets the CLI and GUI share identical
  command-handling logic instead of duplicating it.
- LeBron.getResponse(String) is the new single entry point the GUI
  calls per message; run() (the CLI loop) now calls it too, so both
  interfaces stay in sync automatically.
- New lebron.gui package: Main (the Application, loads
  MainWindow.fxml), Launcher (a plain main() that calls
  Application.launch(), needed because launching an Application
  subclass's own main() directly from the shaded jar can fail
  JavaFX's module-path checks), MainWindow (controller wiring the
  text field/send button to LeBron), and DialogBox (renders one line
  of the conversation as an avatar + label).
- build.gradle: added the org.openjfx dependencies and pointed
  application.mainClass at lebron.gui.Launcher.
- Removed StubUi (no longer needed now that Ui has no I/O side
  effects to stub out) and updated the affected Command/Parser tests
  to assert on the returned response string directly.

Verified with gradlew run, the packaged shadowJar via java -jar, and
gradlew test (all passing).

commitResults.messageTitle: Use Checkstyle to detect coding style violations
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds the Checkstyle Gradle plugin, configured with the SE-EDU
checkstyle.xml/suppressions.xml (copied from se-edu/addressbook-level3),
which enforces the same rules documented at
se-education.org/guides/conventions/java/intermediate.html that were
previously only checked by hand during A-CodingStandard.

Running `gradlew checkstyleMain checkstyleTest` surfaced 14 pre-existing
violations, all now fixed:
- Main.java/MainWindow.java: removed a blank line between the javafx.*
  and lebron.* imports. Neither package matches this config's "org."/
  "com." groups, so both fall into the same import group, and a blank
  line within one group is flagged as extra separation.
- Storage.java: parseTask()'s switch/case was indented flush with the
  switch statement; re-indented case labels and their bodies to match
  this config's caseIndent (case +4, body +4 more).
- ParserTest.java: joined a lambda argument back onto one line, since
  SeparatorWrap requires an opening parenthesis to stay at the end of
  the previous line rather than start a new one, and the lambda's own
  "()" was doing the latter.

`gradlew build` (tests + checkstyle) now passes clean.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use assertions to document code assumptions
commitResults.messageBody:
Several methods relied on invariants that hold only because of how
other classes in this codebase already call them (e.g. Parser always
validates input before constructing a Command or Task), but nothing
in the code itself stated that assumption. If a future change broke
one of these invariants, the resulting bug could surface far from
its actual cause, with nothing explaining what was expected instead.

Add `assert` statements (the Java language feature, not JUnit) at
each such point, so a violation fails fast with a clear message
right where the wrong assumption was made:
- Task/Deadline/Event constructors: description/date fields must be
  non-null (description also non-blank), since Parser is the only
  caller and it already rejects bad input before construction.
- TaskList's constructor and findTasks(): the list/keyword arguments
  must be non-null, for the same reason.
- Storage.parseTask(): a save-format line must carry as many fields
  as its task type requires, since every line we read back was
  written by our own Task#reformat().
- LeBron.getResponse(): every Command must return a non-null reply,
  documenting an implicit contract of the Command interface that all
  nine command classes rely on; also noted in Command's Javadoc.

These deliberately don't duplicate the LeBronException checks that
already validate real user input in Parser - assert is for bugs in
our own code, not for input we can't control, and would be silently
disabled in a normal run anyway.

Verified with a scratch class that these assertions do fire under
`java -ea` (which is also how Gradle's `test` task runs by default)
and are silently skipped without it, matching normal JVM behaviour.
`gradlew build` (tests + checkstyle) still passes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Audited the codebase against the course's Code Quality guidelines
(nus-cs2103-ay2627-s1.github.io/website/se-book-adapted/chapters/codeQuality.html)
and fixed the three clearest violations: magic numbers, duplicated
logic, and a method mixing two levels of abstraction.

- Parser.java: parseTodoDescription/parseDeadlineArgs/parseEventArgs/
  parseFindKeyword each hardcoded a numeric offset (4, 5, 8, 9, 5, 6)
  into input.substring(...), with nothing connecting the number to
  the command keyword it was meant to skip past. Extracted a shared
  extractArgs(input, keyword) helper that computes the offset from
  the keyword's own length, removing both the magic numbers and the
  four copies of near-identical logic.
- Ui.java: showTodoAdded/showDeadlineAdded/showEventAdded/
  showTaskDeleted were copy-paste-modify of the same
  "header + task + count + trailing text" shape, and
  showTaskMarked/showTaskUnmarked likewise duplicated a smaller
  "header + task" shape. Extracted formatTaskMessage() and
  formatTaskCountMessage() helpers so each public method is now a
  one-line call with just its own header text.
- LeBron.getResponse(): the try/if/try nesting for saving after a
  successful command exceeded the "max 3 levels" guideline and mixed
  two levels of abstraction (dispatching a command vs. the mechanics
  of handling a save failure) in one method. Extracted the save
  logic into saveAndGetErrorSuffix(), so getResponse() now reads as
  a flat parse -> execute -> return sequence.

All three refactors are behavior-preserving: gradlew build (full
test suite + Checkstyle) passes unchanged, and no public method
signature or user-visible message text was altered.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Use Streams to replace collection-processing loops
commitResults.messageBody:
Several methods iterated over a List purely to filter, transform, or
concatenate its elements into a result - the kind of operation Java
Streams exist specifically to express more directly, at a single
level of abstraction, instead of managing an explicit accumulator
and loop index by hand.

- TaskList.findTasks(): a plain filter-and-collect over `tasks`.
- TaskList.reformat(): a map (Task -> save-format line) followed by
  concatenation.
- Storage.load(): a filter (skip blank lines) followed by a map
  (line -> Task) followed by collect.
- TaskList.toString() and Ui.showMatchingTasks(): numbered listings,
  which need each element's index. Converted using
  IntStream.range(0, size).mapToObj(...), the standard idiom for
  producing indexed output from a List.

Converting TaskList.reformat()/toString() surfaced a real edge case
worth locking in with a test: for an empty TaskList, the original
loops produced "" directly (zero iterations), which a naive
Collectors.joining(delimiter, prefix, suffix) trick would NOT
reproduce (it still emits the prefix/suffix on an empty stream).
Used `.map(x -> x + "\n").collect(Collectors.joining())` instead,
which naturally returns "" for an empty stream, and added
reformat_emptyList_returnsEmptyString()/toString_emptyList_returnsEmptyString()
to TaskListTest so a future change can't silently reintroduce that
mismatch. Ui.showMatchingTasks()'s empty-match case was already
covered by FindCommandTest's execute_noMatch_reportsEmptyListToUi().

All conversions are behavior-preserving: gradlew build (full test
suite + Checkstyle) passes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Support recurring tasks (e.g. a weekly project meeting)
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds a "recur" command: recur DESCRIPTION every {day|week|month} from
yyyy-MM-dd HHmm, which creates a RecurringTask - a Task that is never
meant to be permanently finished, since something like a weekly
meeting keeps coming back.

Rather than adding a separate "complete this occurrence" command, the
existing "mark" command was made polymorphic instead: Task.setStatus
is overridden in RecurringTask so that marking it done advances its
due date to the next occurrence (day/week/month later) and leaves it
not-done, while unmarking is a no-op. This reuses the command set
everyone already knows instead of growing it, and demonstrates the
Task hierarchy doing real polymorphic work rather than every subclass
just formatting itself differently.

- RecurrenceInterval: a small enum (DAILY/WEEKLY/MONTHLY) that owns
  its own advance(LocalDateTime) date math and fromKeyword(String)
  parsing, so that logic isn't duplicated between RecurringTask and
  Parser.
- RecurringTask: extends Task, overrides setStatus/reformat/toString
  following the same pattern as Deadline/Event.
- RecurringCommand + Parser/CommandType wiring, following the same
  shape as DeadlineCommand/EventCommand.
- Storage: new "R" case in parseTask so recurring tasks persist
  correctly across save/load.
- Ui.showRecurringAdded reuses the existing formatTaskCountMessage
  helper from A-CodeQuality.

Verified with gradlew build (full test suite + Checkstyle) and a
manual end-to-end run through LeBron.getResponse (add -> list -> mark
-> list -> delete) confirming the due date actually advances on mark
while the task stays active.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
